conclusions: Largest observed phase in first-outer sample is logP replay (approximately 65.34%), followed by feedback generation (approximately 24.97%) and full-class gradients (approximately 9.42%).
Native scoring totals approximately 33 seconds in the four first-outer samples; API latency is not supported as the principal bottleneck and registered API_calls is zero.
Ordinary training commits typically arrive approximately every 36 seconds. Completed later outers take approximately 10.24 to 11.69 hours in checkpoint-mtime wall intervals.
OOM failure and administrative resource release add observed delays; their intervals are separately reported and not charged as pure model computation.
V25 binds frozen V18 scientific runtime; later candidate V19 replay changes are not evidence of deployed acceleration in this round.
limitations: No model answers, private test reference values, rewards or dev/test score values were extracted; only metadata scalars and source control flow were used.
FirstOuterAudit instruments step298 only; first-outer phase percentages cannot be generalized as exact whole-run percentages.
Wall-clock phase timing is not GPU profiling; CUDA utilization, CPU overhead and I/O fractions remain unmeasured.
Checkpoint mtimes measure commit spacing, including serialization/I/O; first-to-last step interval excludes the first step computation.
Ordinary-step interval distribution excludes registered adaptive outer boundaries, not arbitrary slow steps.
Later-outer intervals start from the same-step training checkpoint; initial branch-to-outer intervals with failures/queue are deliberately excluded.
Worker launch-to-exit includes initialization and controller polling. Controller adoption events are not treated as fresh starts.
Generation run.json may predate actual worker dispatch; its mtime is deliberately not used as test generation start.
Failure-to-restart and administrative gaps are observed wall-clock intervals, not measured wasted GPU hours or exclusively engineering labor.
Ongoing outer/replay work has no end timestamp; no runtime is extrapolated past the verified memory-hold cutoff.
Optimizer-step completion fraction excludes partial work and is not a wall-clock completion percentage; outer costs dominate observed adaptive runs.
